methodology.metaDescription: vpncompaire evaluates every VPN against six objective criteria: privacy, independent audits, speed, streaming compatibility, pricing transparency and ease of use.
methodology.intro: Every VPN on the site is evaluated against the same six objective criteria. Affiliate commission does not influence rankings or scores. Below we explain how each criterion is measured — transparency is the prerequisite of trust.

privacy.title: Privacy policy and jurisdiction
privacy.body: We evaluate the provider's logging policy, the country its headquarters is in (5/9/14 Eyes alliances, data retention laws) and how it responds to legal requests. Jurisdiction determines how strongly a no-logs claim is actually protected.

audits.title: Independent audits
audits.body: The presence, frequency and scope of third-party audit reports (Deloitte, KPMG, Cure53, Securitum, Assured AB, etc.) drive the weight of this criterion. Court-proven no-logs (e.g. PIA) earns the highest score.

speed.title: Speed
speed.body: We run real speed tests against the same baseline at near, medium and far server distances. WireGuard and proprietary protocols (Lightway, NordLynx) are scored separately. Peak-hour performance is also checked.

streaming.title: Streaming compatibility
streaming.body: Access tests on platforms like Netflix US/UK/TR, Disney+, BBC iPlayer, BluTV and Exxen using different servers. Providers that are persistently blocked score lower.

pricing.title: Pricing transparency
pricing.body: The gap between the first-purchase price and the renewal price, hidden fees, the real money-back policy, and the genuine monthly cost of long-term plans are all reviewed.

usability.title: Ease of use
usability.body: App interface, initial setup time, server-picker ergonomics, auto-connect rules and customer-support accessibility (live chat, response time) are all assessed.

editorial.title: Editorial independence
editorial.body: We disclose affiliate revenue transparently (see <link>Advertising Disclosure</link>). VPN providers without an affiliate programme are also included in our ranking; this is the most direct signal of our impartiality.

calculator.metaDescription: Compare the true 1, 2 or 3-year total cost of 10 VPNs. First-term discount + renewal price included. Effective monthly price and savings.
calculator.ogDescription: Calculate the real 3-year VPN cost, renewal included.
calculator.intro: Most VPNs are cheap up front and expensive on renewal. Here you see the true 1/2/3-year total cost — compare fairly on "effective monthly" price.

tool.explanation: How it's calculated: discounted first-term price, then monthly-plan price on renewal. Most providers use a "renewal trap" — cheap up front, 2–3× more after. Disabling auto-renew and re-buying on discount saves money.

howSection.calcBody: For each VPN we take the "best value" plan (typically 2–3 years) as the reference. During the plan term the discounted price applies; after it expires we assume renewal at the monthly-plan rate. This is the source of most Trustpilot complaints — users see "$30 the first year, $120 the second year."
howSection.trapTitle: How to dodge the renewal trap
howSection.trap1Body: — log in to your VPN account and turn off auto-renew in billing settings.
howSection.trap2Body: buy a fresh discounted plan from the same provider or a different one.
howSection.trap3Body: — flat €5/month, no discount/renewal trap. Better for consistency than for squeezing out savings.
howSection.term1Body: The right balance for most users — meaningful discount, manageable commitment.
howSection.term2Body: Lowest effective monthly, but a 3-year commitment to one provider. The VPN market moves fast — even cheap is risky.
howSection.term3Body: Flexibility but 2–3× more expensive. Only for short-term needs.

about.metaDescription: What vpncompaire is, why it exists and how it works. A volunteer review project with editorial independence and a transparent methodology.
about.lede: The VPN world is confusing: hundreds of providers, contradicting reviews, aggressive marketing. {site} started as a personal response to that mess — a volunteer review project.

explainer.title: What is this?
explainer.body: {site} is not a company or institution; it has no registered legal entity. It is a public version of the notes that built up while we were comparing VPN providers for our own use. Affiliate commissions cover infrastructure costs; they do not influence the recommendations. See <disclosure>Advertising disclosure</disclosure> and <legal>Legal notice</legal> for details.

approach.body: We try to make it easier to find clear, independent, methodology-driven information when choosing a VPN. Our assessments come from independent audit reports, public sources and our own test observations — not marketing copy. No recommendation is a hard guarantee; the final decision is always yours.

transparent.title: Transparent methodology
transparent.body: Every VPN is scored against the same six criteria. The criteria and their weights are public.

independence.title: Editorial independence
independence.body: Affiliate commissions do not influence the ranking or the assessment. We also list providers without an affiliate programme.

evidence.title: Evidence first
evidence.body: Saying "good VPN" isn't enough — independent audits, court rulings or audit reports are required.

howWeTest.body: Every VPN on the site is evaluated against the same six objective criteria: privacy policy and jurisdiction, independent audits, speed, streaming compatibility, pricing transparency and ease of use. See our <methodology>methodology page</methodology> for the details.

revenue.body1: We finance this site through affiliate commissions. When you buy a VPN through a link on this page we earn a commission — the price you pay doesn't change. We explain this in detail on the <disclosure>Advertising disclosure</disclosure> page.
revenue.body2: Important: Differences in commission do not influence the ranking. We include providers that don't run an affiliate programme (e.g. Mullvad); we don't put the highest-commission product at the top.

authors.body: {site} started as a personal project. Content is produced through volunteer contributions; there is no professional newsroom or editorial staff. The primary sources are providers' own audit reports, publicly available court documents, open-source repositories and our own observations. If you find anything wrong or missing, please let us know — we take corrections seriously.

why.body: Commercial VPN reviews are mostly sales-driven; "best" claims get repeated without sources. {site} is a reference project that started as a hobby and grew more systematic over time, written into that gap. The goal is not to give a single "correct answer" — it's to provide structured information so the reader can make their own call.

contactSection.body: For feedback, correction requests or questions, visit our <contact>contact page</contact>.
